name: Saltmere Reach

stars.name: Saltmere
stars.notes: A steady sun-like star midway through a quiet middle age; its light falls on the brine-world below with almost nostalgic evenness, which is precisely why the colonies chose it.

planets.name: Kiln
planets.notes: A blistered forge-world skimming the star; automated sulfur skimmers brave its orbit for industrial reagents and lose one in twenty trips.

planets.name: Ballast Stone
planets.notes: A cratered airless rock worked by teleoperated mines; its nickel fed the orbital yards during the colonization wave and still does.

planets.name: Saltmere Prime
planets.notes: A world-girdling brine ocean dotted with three hundred million people across floating harbor-cities, terraced kelp reefs, and the Grand Lock, the largest free-port structure outside the coreward routes.

planets.name: Farthing
planets.notes: A scrappy frontier colony of coastal farmsteads and one stubborn starport; its settlers broke from Combine charter control and have been in tariff dispute ever since.

planets.name: Grave Sand
planets.notes: A wind-scoured dune world with trace salt flats; prospectors keep testing its basins for ancient seabeds and keep finding only older sand.

planets.name: Cask
planets.notes: A barrel-banded tan giant supplying the system's helium-3; skimming platforms on its moons anchor the fuel trade that keeps the Reach's traffic moving.

planets.name: Second Cask
planets.notes: A colder hydrogen sibling with a thin, glittering ring; patrol squadrons from both factions stage on its far side and pretend not to see each other.

planets.name: Whitlow
planets.notes: A groaning ice shell world whose tidal cracks vent vapor geysers; research buoys drift through its plumes sampling for organics.

planets.name: Last Buoy
planets.notes: A frozen pebble at the system's edge carrying the navigation buoy that names the Reach; tradition holds you touch your hull to it before jumping rimward.

asteroid_belts.name: The Shambles
asteroid_belts.notes: A working belt of ore claims and derelict rigging; customs cutters patrol its lanes and pirates nest in its shadows with equal diligence.

asteroid_belts.name: Ice Rigging
asteroid_belts.notes: A thin halo of comet fragments harvested for volatiles by Farthing's independent water-runners.

stations.name: Grand Lock of Saltmere
stations.notes: The immense free-port ring where ocean freighters, kelp barques, and coreward liners moor side by side; a quarter million souls live on its tide-decks and answer to no single flag.

stations.name: Quarantine Gate
stations.notes: The Combine customs fortress watching Farthing's starport; its boarding cutters enforce tariff law and its brig holds the ones who argued.

stations.name: Slack-Water Depot
stations.notes: A neutral fuel and salvage depot buried in the belt, where Combine and League captains drink in the same bar and check their sidearms at the door.

faction_control.notes: The Meridian Combine holds Saltmere Prime's port charters and Quarantine Gate; the Freehold League arms Farthing and the belt depots. Open battle hasn't started, but the tariff war is real and the Shambles is where it will ignite.

history: Survey crews following the coreward current routes found Saltmere Prime's warm brine seas in the great expansion years, and within a decade the first harbor-cities were welding hull-to-hull above the swells.

The Combine consolidated the kelp and fuel trades under one port charter, provoking Farthing's settler rebellion and the founding of the Freehold League, whose water-runners still defy Combine tariffs belt by belt.
Last quarter the Combine doubled transit fees at the Grand Lock; League convoys began routing through the Ice Rigging in protest, and three customs cutters have gone missing in the Shambles since.
description: A patient yellow star shines on nine orderly orbits, but everything worth having in Saltmere Reach flows around the third: a vast brine ocean flecked with floating cities, terraced kelp reefs visible from orbit, and the Grand Lock, a port ring so large it casts a tide of shadow across the swells below. Rocky inner worlds, two fuel-rich giants, and a rimward scatter of ice complete a system built like a well-found ship.

This is the busiest crossroads in the Meridian Wash, where coreward liners, kelp barques, and helium tankers crowd the approach lanes and a quarter million people live on the Grand Lock alone. The Meridian Combine runs the port and the customs guns of Quarantine Gate; the Freehold League runs Farthing, the water-runners, and an increasingly bold fleet of armed freighters. Traffic never stops, and neither does the argument over who taxes it.

Beneath the bustle, the water grows deeper and stranger. Saltmere Prime's abyssal trenches return sonar echoes shaped like architecture, Whitlow's geyser plumes carry complex organics nobody will fund a mission to confirm, and the missing customs cutters in the Shambles left no debris. Old harbor-pilots say the ocean world keeps its own ledgers, and lately, they claim, the balance has begun to change.
